THE REASON HAS A NAME - Goodhart's law. The equation's own 'made measurable' section defines Hi (integrity, the negative feedback path) as promised-vs-delivered. The workgraph's closure model computes exactly that shape. If the graph could SEE that closing a node raises Hi, closure stops measuring integrity and becomes a score to farm - the measure becomes a target and ceases to be a good measure. Dormancy is not aesthetic caution; it is what keeps the reading honest. WHAT ALIGNS, unprompted (the equation predates every one of these surfaces): Hi promised-vs-delivered maps to the closure model; epsilon, the MASTER METRIC, |forecast - actual|, maps to the corrections lane - a correction is a prediction error made explicit, and this capture has six of them verified across four amend passes; G, open-loop gain / new qualified opportunities, maps to the rate at which the findings and suggested lanes surface work; Hr, the reputation path / share arriving BECAUSE of prior work, maps to the share of new nodes that attach to existing ones by edge rather than arriving unconnected. Four proxies, none of which anyone designed to match. THE CONTRACT, four rules that make it dormant rather than participating: (1) the observer READS the workgraph and never writes to it - no node, no edge, no field, no flag; (2) the workgraph carries ZERO reference to the equation, which is testable - grep the graph data for 'equation' and it must return nothing; (3) the observer publishes its own surface, derived only; (4) the moment the observer needs a field added to the graph, it has stopped being dormant and that is the signal to stop, not to add the field. HONEST SCOPE, and this one matters because the equation is Gavin's family's story: its real instrumentation is MONTHLY, across income, milestones and opportunities, with the family check-in as the measurement tick. The workgraph proxies are a different domain at a different scale. They demonstrate that the SHAPES align; they do not measure his life. The observer surface says so on its face.

The DGS header tiles fetch the workgraph JSON and swap innerHTML. The Meridian day surface recomputes counts. griot-viz-engine emits shell/isometric/nodegraph with no shared clock. Liveline names the discipline that would make them feel like one instrument instead of several widgets - and it is a ~single-file technique, not a framework to adopt. Features beyond the core: momentum arrows, time-window buttons, candlestick toggle, multi-series, loading and paused states, automatic palette generation from a theme colour. nodes.title: Agentation x Kweli - the comprehension-and-approval seam, and griot-viz-engine as its natural evolution
nodes.description: Gavin's call 2026-09-13: 'agentation and kweli go hand in hand... not to mention griot-viz-engine and kweli is the natural evolution.' Agentation (benjitaylor/agentation, 4.5k stars, npm install agentation -D, React 18+, zero external dependencies) is a visual annotation layer for AI coding agents: you click a rendered element and it captures the selector, the class names, the DOM position and the bounding box; you select text and the exact string travels; you drag to multi-select or to mark empty space for layout feedback; and - the detail that matters most - it FREEZES CSS animations mid-sequence so an ephemeral state can be annotated at all. Output is plain markdown with selectors at four escalating detail levels: compact (selector + note), standard (adds position and selected text), detailed (adds bounding boxes and context), forensic (adds computed CSS). His framing of the gap it closes: 'make the avatar smaller' does not identify which element or how much. WHY THIS IS KWELI'S SEAM: Kweli is the comprehension-and-approval platform. Agentation is approval capture with structured evidence attached - a human points at the thing, and what travels onward is a machine-addressable record rather than a sentence. That is the same primitive, aimed at agents instead of at people. AND THE EVOLUTION GAVIN NAMES: griot-viz-engine renders the artifact; Kweli captures the approval on what was rendered; the four detail levels are the fidelity ladder the viz engine ALREADY has (lo / mid / hi). Render, point, approve, with the evidence carried. Licence recorded for the shipping gate, not for now: PolyForm Shield 1.0.0.

nodes.title: griot-workgraph-update can add and correct nodes but cannot advance a node's state
nodes.description: amend-workgraph.mjs is idempotent on node id: a node that already exists is skipped entirely. So there is no supported way to move a node from named-unfiled to done when the work simply LANDS and nothing was ever wrong. Deliberately NOT built here: extending Gavin's engine unasked is inventing his tool's interface, the same call made on the griot-gold-log SKILL.md.

nodes.title: A suggestion with no readiness block renders as a red 0% card, reading as failure rather than as unassessed
nodes.description: The suggested-lane renderer defaults a missing readiness to {score:0} and colours anything under 65 with the miss hue. S7 was filed in amendPass26 without a readiness assessment, so the moment the lane started rendering (after the scope fix in C3/N42) it would have shown Gavin a red zero against a suggestion that had simply never been scored. Unassessed and failing must not look the same on a decision surface - that is the entire argument for the measured/judged tagging in the readiness model.

verification.evidence: Renderer at djeli-branch-capture-codex.html line 427: var r = n.readiness || {factors:{}, score:0, measured:{}}; line 428 selects var(--miss) for score < 65. Graph query confirmed S1-S6 each carry a readiness block and S7 did not. Fixed in this pass by scoring S7 against the declared readinessModel to 86, weakest factor decision debt at 10.
verification.result: verified and fixed - S7 now carries a decomposable score whose lowest factor names the actual blocker, per the readinessModel rule

nodes.title: The two 'cards ahead of repo' were a measurement artifact, not lost content (closed by C15)
nodes.description: The gate refuses to publish repo-over-card when the card is bigger, because that direction could destroy content rather than refresh it. Two cards sit in that state. The likeliest explanation is benign - the publish pipeline wraps the HTML and adds roughly a kilobyte - in which case the repo is the truth and they can be republished like any other. But the alternative is that a card was edited or published from a newer source that never made it back to the repo, in which case publishing over it would delete work. The ask is whether Gavin wants the delta diffed and reconciled into the repo first, or the wrapper hypothesis confirmed once and the pair treated as noise forever. Never inferred: only he knows whether either card was ever edited outside the repo path.

verification.evidence: Common prefix/suffix diff proved the repo file equals the card minus its injected meta block, exactly, for both pairs. After the fix: 'in sync (body hash match) : 90 / STALE 0 / NO CARD 0 / card ahead of repo 0'.
verification.result: closed - resolved by measuring correctly, not by choosing a side

correction.wasClaimed: Two cards are LARGER than their repo files (fastapi-vs-flask-kente, prism-channel-rollout-status) - the gate refuses to publish over them, awaiting Gavin's ruling on which side is authoritative.
correction.isTrue: There was nothing to rule on. Both card bodies were byte-identical to their repo files; the extra ~510 bytes were the cowork-artifact-meta block the publish pipeline injects. The gate was comparing a wrapped file against an unwrapped one using size, so it reported content loss that never happened.
correction.cause: verify-cards.ps1 compared size and mtime while claiming to SHA-256. Closed by C15: the wrapper is stripped and the body hashed, and both entries now report in sync.

nodes.title: The amend helper silently dropped every correction field outside a four-key allowlist
nodes.description: amend-workgraph.mjs validated a correction's wasClaimed/isTrue/cause, then applied only description, title, verification and group to the node before stamping the correction block. Every other field a correction carried - readiness, state, direction, outputs - was discarded without a refusal, so the run printed 'corrections: <target>' and the value never landed. The skill's own documented contract is '{target, wasClaimed, isTrue, cause} plus whatever fields it replaces', so the engine had been quietly narrower than its spec. This is the graph's own invariant turned on itself: a correction that cannot change the thing it corrects is a silent overwrite of the correction, not of the node.

verification.evidence: amend-workgraph.mjs lines 51-53 applied description/title/verification, line 58-61 group, line 62 stamped node.correction - no generic pass. Proven empirically in amendPass27: the S7 readiness correction reported 'corrections: wg:djeli-branch:S7' and exited 0, then a graph query returned S7 keys = id, originLane, outputs, contractPath, localId, kind, group, state, direction, title, description, verification, correction - readiness absent, and the lane still rendered it as an unscored 0%. Fixed by applying any non-RESERVED key generically, with originLane/id/localId protected as identity and immutable.
verification.result: verified - defect reproduced in a real pass, patched in the digital-griot-skills canonical and the ~/.claude/skills deployment, both node --check clean

nodes.title: The skills canonical and its deployment differ only by line endings - not the sixth propagation drift it looked like
nodes.description: A hash compare of griot-workgraph-update/scripts between the digital-griot-skills canonical and the ~/.claude/skills deployment showed all four files mismatching, with the DEPLOYED copies newer than the canonical - which reads exactly like ungated propagation target drift in its most dangerous direction, source-of-truth behind its own deployment. A line-by-line diff showed zero content differences on all three unpatched scripts: the mismatch is CRLF versus LF. Recorded as a reframe rather than a finding of drift, because acting on the hash alone would have 'reconciled' a divergence that does not exist and could have regressed a working engine.

verification.evidence: Get-FileHash mismatch on amend-workgraph.mjs, backfill-verification.mjs, sync-codex-data.mjs and verify-workgraph.mjs, with deployed mtimes 2026-09-15 07:15 against canonical 2026-09-13. Compare-Object on the line arrays of all three unpatched files returned zero differing lines. The apparent newness of the deployment is a redeploy-copy timestamp, not an edit.
verification.result: verified - hash inequality explained entirely by line-ending normalisation; no content drift, no reconciliation needed

nodes.title: The shadow-DOM mirror-tab rewrite was built, shipped, and REVERTED the same hour
nodes.description: An attempt to make the five DGS mirror tabs render on every surface by replacing their iframes with shadow-DOM inlines. It cleared every Content Security Policy error it set out to clear and was still WRONG: the workgraph mirror rendered without the lines between its nodes, and the ontology mirror replaced its interactive map with a dependency banner. Gavin caught it on sight and named the governing rule - we do not replace visually good things with broken upgrades. Reverted to the iframe build at 4b320bc. Recorded as a branch that shipped and was pulled, not as a success, because the record of having been wrong is the point.

verification.evidence: Published build 92d8d9c logged only two cosmetic Google-Fonts style-src errors at 16:06:52Z - no frame-src, no connect-src, no EvalError - and the Playwright gate returned ok:true, problems:[], errs:[]. Both signals were green while the rendered page was visibly degraded: screenshot from Gavin shows the ontology tab displaying the vendored-dependency notice in place of its map, and he reported the workgraph mirror drawing no edges between nodes. Reverted by restoring live/dgs-definitive-plan.html from 4c6dab6 (5 iframes restored, 0 payload blocks, wgstats inline and viz-templates preserved), committed 4b320bc and republished.
verification.result: reverted - the surface is back to the iframe build; the rewrite is recorded as attempted-and-withdrawn rather than shipped

nodes.title: Both gates measured absence of errors and called it correctness
nodes.description: Two independent checks passed a visibly broken build. Playwright asserted mount status, element counts and console errors; verify_artifact asserted the console log on the real surface. Neither asserted that the thing LOOKED right, so a workgraph with no edges and an ontology with no map sailed through both. The deeper cause is that the workgraph codex traces its edges between the measured positions of rendered chips, and a shadow root inside an inactive tab yields zero-size layout boxes - a failure that produces no error at all, just nothing drawn. Counting elements cannot detect it. Flagged not fixed: the gate needs a visual assertion (screenshot diff, or asserting non-zero geometry on the drawn edges) before any further attempt at this class of change.

verification.evidence: verify-mirrors.mjs assertions were: mounted, chars, element count, styleKB, scriptError - no geometry, no pixels. It returned workgraph mounted:true chars:184335 els:2022 scriptError:null for the build whose edges were missing. The artifact debug log for the same build at 16:06:52Z carried only two style-src entries. The defect was found by a human looking at the screen, which is the only check that caught it.
verification.result: verified - the failure is reproducible in both harnesses as a PASS, which is precisely the problem

nodes.title: Four live codexes depend on CDN libraries and cannot fully run in the artifact sandbox
nodes.description: Scanning every live/*.html for external script tags found four: griot-ontology-codex and griot-suite-map pull d3, gavel-decision-review pulls React + ReactDOM + Babel, kweli-brand-matrix pulls html2canvas. The artifact sandbox's script-src permits only self, inline and three named jsdelivr bundles, so none of these load there. This is why the ontology tab cannot be made equivalent by inlining alone - d3 creates its map nodes, so without d3 vendored there is no map, only prose. It also means the iframe is currently the ONLY way those codexes render correctly anywhere, which is an argument for leaving the iframes alone until a library is actually vendored.

verification.evidence: Regex over live/*.html for external script src: griot-ontology-codex.html and griot-suite-map.html -> d3.min.js; gavel-decision-review.html -> react.production.min.js, react-dom.production.min.js, babel.min.js; kweli-brand-matrix.html -> html2canvas.min.js. Dependency confirmed load-bearing for the ontology codex: its script calls document.getElementById for 'anodes', 'aedges' and 'amap', and none of those ids exist anywhere in the file - d3 creates them at runtime.
verification.result: verified - four files, named libraries, and the ontology case traced from missing ids to the library that creates them

nodes.title: A codex storing entity-encoded markup renders under the document parser and breaks under innerHTML
nodes.description: The ontology codex stores its SVG map with HTML entities in attribute position (id="amap", viewBox="0 0 1000 620"). The document parser handles that the way it always has, so the standalone codex is clean. Assigning the same markup through innerHTML re-decodes those entities inside attributes and yields backslash-quoted SVG values the browser rejects. DOMParser, which is what the standalone page effectively uses, handles it correctly. Kept even though the change that surfaced it was reverted, because the fact is about the FILE and will bite any future attempt to embed it - and because the reflex on seeing those errors is to assume the codex is malformed, which it is not.

verification.evidence: Baseline run loading griot-ontology-codex.html and djeli-branch-capture-codex.html standalone in Playwright: 0 console errors each, proving the seven SVG attribute errors (viewBox, markerWidth, markerHeight, refX, refY, orient, path d) were introduced by innerHTML rather than inherited. Replacing innerHTML with DOMParser().parseFromString + node adoption removed all seven while the element count held at 224.
verification.result: verified in both directions - reproduced with innerHTML, absent with DOMParser, standalone baseline proving it was not pre-existing

nodes.title: Restoring the edit base from HEAD silently re-verified the previous build
nodes.description: The rebuild loop restored its base with git checkout HEAD. Once a build had been committed, HEAD ALREADY contained the change, so the builder's idempotency guard printed 'ALREADY INLINED - no-op' and the gate then verified the OLD build while appearing to verify the new one. The base for a rebuild must be the last commit WITHOUT the change, never HEAD. Fixed by walking the file's history for the newest change-free commit, with an explicit refusal if the resolved base still contains it.

verification.evidence: Observed directly: after committing 74a673f, a rebuild reported 'nothing to commit, working tree clean' and the gate returned ok:true on a build that had not been regenerated. The base-finder then needed two corrections of its own - git show returns an ARRAY of lines, so -notmatch filtered instead of testing and every commit read as change-free; and the pathspec needed forward slashes. Per-commit audit after the fix: b914984 True, 74a673f True, 4c6dab6 False -> base correctly resolved to 4c6dab6.
verification.result: verified - the guard refused a bad base out loud before the fix and resolved the correct one after

nodes.title: Do the Cowork mirror tabs need fixing at all, or is claude.ai the surface that matters for them?
nodes.description: The iframes render correctly on claude.ai and blank in Cowork. Today's attempt to make them universal produced a version that rendered everywhere and correctly nowhere, so the honest question is whether the Cowork gap is worth closing. Three real options, and the choice is Gavin's because it is about where he actually reads the plan. ONE: leave the iframes, treat claude.ai as the canonical surface for mirror tabs, and say so in the skills - costs nothing, keeps the good view. TWO: pre-render each codex to static HTML with Playwright at publish time and inline THAT, which preserves appearance because the picture is already drawn, at the cost of losing interactivity inside the tab and adding a render step. THREE: vendor the CDN libraries and fix the layout-timing problem, the most faithful and by far the most work. Never inferred: option one may simply be correct, and the failed attempt is evidence for it rather than against it.

verification.evidence: Measured today: the iframe build renders correctly on claude.ai and produces five frame-src denials in the Cowork sandbox. The shadow-DOM build cleared every CSP error and lost the workgraph edges and the ontology map. N45 establishes that two of the five codexes cannot run their graphs in the sandbox at all without vendored libraries.
verification.result: open - deliberately unresolved; the revert restored the status quo so the decision is not under time pressure

nodes.title: rebuild-dgs-mirrors.ps1 - refuses to commit while the gate is red
nodes.description: Written the moment after a commit landed with the gate still failing. Its value is not convenience, it is ORDER: it refuses a dirty tree, resolves the correct pre-change base, builds, runs the visual gate, and commits only on exit 0 - then proves the marker is in HEAD rather than the working copy. It also prints the reminder that file:// carries no CSP, so the harness can never be mistaken for the surface.

verification.evidence: griot-live-artifacts/rebuild-dgs-mirrors.ps1 with tools/inline-mirror-tabs.js and tools/verify-mirrors.mjs, committed a31ff35. Every refusal path exercised for real in-session: refused a dirty tree; refused a base that still contained the change; failed the build loudly on a syntax error and restored the base; and on the good build ran the gate, committed, pushed and confirmed marker-in-HEAD. Dry run without -Commit built and gated without writing.
verification.result: verified - four distinct refusal paths exercised, not asserted

nodes.title: dgs-sync-all.ps1 - one gated command behind /dgs-plan-update
nodes.description: Gavin named this the biggest open gap: the plan updated and nothing downstream of it synced. The branch workgraph, its canonical copy in Prism, the rendered branch codex, the eight mirror files the plan embeds, prism-codex-plan-sync and the other repos were all left to memory, so the master could sit ahead of every surface it summarises and nothing failed. This walks them in dependency order and gates each stage: workgraph three-copy parity, mirrors present and eager, freshness stamp, codex-plan-sync lag, artifact cards by git-commit-time, then a push of every repo proven by ref equality. It ends by PRINTING the card-publish list it cannot perform, because the artifact tool lives in the session and not in PowerShell - naming what it cannot do rather than implying it did.

verification.evidence: griot-live-artifacts/dgs-sync-all.ps1. First dry run: 5 stages green, artifact-cards FAIL naming dgs-definitive-plan 16 KB behind, exit 1, DGS_SYNC_INCOMPLETE. -Commit run pushed griot-live-artifacts 799ddb7, Prism 640393f, griot-ontology and digital-griot-skills, each confirmed local HEAD == origin/main, and still reported INCOMPLETE for the unpublished card rather than claiming done. Wired into dgs-plan-update SKILL.md as Step 7 in BOTH the digital-griot-skills canonical and the ~/.claude/skills deployment (41,473 bytes each).
verification.result: verified - the gate failed the run that built it, which is the same proof C7 earned

nodes.title: The plan's own header claimed a date five days older than the file
nodes.description: The DGS header read 'updated 2026-09-12' on a file that had been rewritten that morning - a hardcoded stamp in the one place whose entire job is to say how current the page is. The plan's own guidance already said prefer computed over hardcoded; the header was the exception nobody had noticed. Fixed with an instant in data-stamp written by the sync run and a relative chip recomputed on EVERY page load and re-ticked every 30s, colour-graded fresh/stale/old. The deeper point: a hardcoded date cannot tell you it has gone stale, and a relative one cannot avoid it.

verification.evidence: Header at line 369 carried <span id="hdUpdated" data-stamp="2026-09-12"> while the file's git mtime was 2026-09-17. After the fix, verified in chrome-devtools by forcing the stamp across the range: 3m -> '3 minutes ago' [fresh], 90m -> '2 hours ago' [fresh], 2d -> '2 days ago' [stale], 20d -> '3 weeks ago' [old]. A second defect surfaced and was fixed in the same check: a sibling script wrote the raw ISO instant into the visible text, so the header read 'updated 2026-09-17T16:37:04.776Z'; the ticker now normalises it to the date. Pattern extracted to viz-templates/templates/06-freshness-header.html.
verification.result: verified in a browser across four time bands, not asserted

nodes.title: The sync script corrupted the plan it exists to keep honest - and the damage compounded
nodes.description: dgs-sync-all.ps1 stamped the plan every run using Get-Content -Raw, which on Windows PowerShell 5.1 reads with the ANSI codepage (1252), not UTF-8. Writing it back as UTF-8 re-encoded every multi-byte character. One run turns a middot into two chars; three runs turned the DGS header into unreadable noise and Gavin saw it before any gate did. The failure is silent (no error, no exit code), it MULTIPLIES per run, and the offender was the orchestrator whose whole purpose is keeping surfaces honest. A repair tool that corrupts what it repairs is worse than no tool.

verification.evidence: Fingerprinted the compounding directly: commit 1d82a3e clean, 799ddb7 3666 artefacts, 1994db9 9705, a5fdab6 23903. Repaired by strict cp1252-encode/utf8-decode (throws rather than guesses) converging in 4 passes with zero U+FFFD, then 11 residual single-pass artefacts fixed by literal map. Root cause fixed with Read-Utf8/Write-Utf8 helpers pinned to UTF8Encoding(false); stage 0 gate added; the stamp stage now re-checks its own write and calls Die if it corrupted anything.
verification.result: verified in chrome-devtools on the rendered page - 0 mojibake in body text, title renders 'Digital Griot Suite - Definitive Planning', 21 tabs, 8 mirrors

nodes.title: 13 files were already corrupted before today, and nothing was looking
nodes.description: Gavin refused to let the plan-only fix stand: 'if any other ones exist that are messed up even before today I would like to fix it rather than kicking the can down the road.' The sweep found 14 dirty files in 6,776 - including the branch codex at 89 artefacts and the CANONICAL workgraph index at 102. The codex damage sat entirely in the hand-authored page chrome, zero in the synced data block, which proves the renderer was innocent and the template carried the wound. The lesson generalises: when you find one instance of a class, sweep for the class.

verification.evidence: tools/sweep-mojibake.mjs over 6,776 files. 8 files literal-repaired; Prism/.prism/shared/workgraph/index.json repaired JSON-aware per string value (12 strings, structure re-parsed, key count preserved) because whole-file decode refused. Re-sweep returns dirty=0. Three files are allowlisted - dgs-sync-all.ps1, widget-internals.md, cl-viz-export/SKILL.md - because they quote the artefact on purpose; repairing them would delete the lesson.
verification.result: verified - dirty=0 across 6,776 files on re-sweep

nodes.title: The first gate to fail crashed the reporter instead of reporting
nodes.description: Die() calls Report(), but Report was defined eighty lines further down. PowerShell resolves functions at call time in source order, so the moment the new encoding gate actually fired, the script threw CommandNotFoundException instead of printing which stage failed. A gate that cannot report its own failure is not a gate - it is a crash with good intentions. Found only because the new gate fired on its very first run.

verification.evidence: Run output: "Report : The term 'Report' is not recognized" at dgs-sync-all.ps1:64 immediately after [FAIL] plan encoding intact. Report hoisted above Die with a comment explaining the ordering constraint; subsequent runs print the full SUMMARY block on both the red and the green path.
verification.result: verified - the next failing run printed its summary instead of crashing

nodes.title: The freshness stamp manufactured the drift it then reported
nodes.description: Stage 3 rewrote the plan's stamp on EVERY run, which re-dirtied the file and instantly made the published card stale - so stage 5 could never be green and DGS_SYNC_OK was unreachable by construction. A check must not manufacture the condition it checks. Now the stamp fires only when the plan has real uncommitted changes; an unchanged plan keeps its stamp and the run can converge.

verification.evidence: Before: every -Commit run ended DGS_SYNC_INCOMPLETE on 'artifact cards current' with exactly one stale card, the plan itself. After the change-gate: 'plan freshness stamp OK 2026-09-17T16:50:52.991Z (plan had 1 uncommitted change(s))' and the run reached DGS_SYNC_OK with all four repos ref-equal.
verification.result: verified - first fully green DGS_SYNC_OK run

nodes.title: tools/sweep-mojibake.mjs - repair that is provable or refuses
nodes.description: The ecosystem encoding gate, wired into dgs-sync-all.ps1 as stage 0b so it runs on every sync rather than being a thing someone remembers. It encodes strict-cp1252 and decodes strict-utf8, so an unmappable character or an invalid sequence THROWS instead of silently producing U+FFFD. That matters because the earlier ad-hoc 'fix' is exactly what deepened the corruption: a guess that looks like a repair. It also carries an allowlist, because three files in the suite document this bug by quoting it.

verification.evidence: griot-live-artifacts/tools/sweep-mojibake.mjs. Detect run found 14 dirty; --fix repaired 13 and left the allowlisted three; re-sweep dirty=0. Refusal path exercised for real on Prism's workgraph index.json, which the whole-file decoder declined (102 -> 84) and which was then repaired per JSON string value instead of being forced. Wired as stage 0b; stage 0 guards the plan specifically.
verification.result: verified - both the repair path and the refusal path exercised on real files

nodes.title: The hub is one system: plan + reflect + codexes all feed the global and branch workgraphs
nodes.description: Gavin named the architecture out loud: the DGS Definitive Plan is the source of truth and is being prepared to mount inside Djeli; dgs-plan-update, griot-meridian-reflect, the codexes and the mirrors are not separate rituals but lanes feeding the global workgraph and the branch workgraph, with the plan as the surface that shows them as one thing. He also set the standing obligation - every task we do gets recorded in both graphs, not just the notable ones. Both are now ontology sections, propagated to every surface in the same pass.

verification.evidence: Two sections added to griot-ontology/claude/CLAUDE.md: 'encoding - PowerShell 5.1 reads ANSI, and the damage COMPOUNDS' and 'every task lands in the workgraph AND the branch workgraph'. propagate.ps1 (itself repaired to read UTF-8 rather than ANSI) synced GLOBAL, the agent-ontology compat mirror and .codex/AGENTS.md; canonical and global copies hash-identical at 77498FC6F7A6, 67,647 bytes, both sections present.
verification.result: verified by sha256 parity across copies, not by assertion

nodes.title: Meridian is now a gated stage in the sync spine (closed by C14)
nodes.description: dgs-sync-all.ps1 walks workgraph, mirrors, stamp, codex-plan-sync, cards and repos - but not the Meridian lane. griot-meridian-reflect writes Going Dark and Day Surface and feeds the same graphs, so it can drift from the hub exactly the way the artifact cards did before the card gate existed. Gavin raised the interconnection explicitly while this was being built. Needs a gated Meridian stage plus an edge in the graph.

verification.evidence: dgs-sync-all.ps1 stage list now reads: 0 encoding, 0b ecosystem sweep, 1 workgraph parity, 2 mirrors, 3 stamp, 4 prism codex-plan-sync, 4b surface registry + meridian, 5 push, 6 cards. Run output: '[OK  ] surface registry + meridian   9 surfaces owned, embedded, current'.
verification.result: closed - verified by the run that closed it

correction.wasClaimed: Meridian is not yet a stage in the sync spine - griot-meridian-reflect feeds the same graphs but dgs-sync-all.ps1 does not touch that lane, so it can drift from the hub the way the artifact cards did.
correction.isTrue: Closed. Stage 4b (surface registry + meridian) now walks the SURFACES registry and holds the reflect lane, checking channel-going-dark and channel-day-surface by parsed newest-entry key against the 4am day boundary.
correction.cause: Named and scoped in the same session it was built, then closed once C14 shipped and the full sync reported 'surface registry + meridian OK - 9 surfaces owned, embedded, current'.

nodes.title: The SURFACES registry - nine mirrors declared as one system
nodes.description: Gavin: 'the Dashboard and the ecosystem dashboard and the day surface and parts of the briefing seem disconnected when they all operate different parts of the same system and are equally important.' They were. Nine mirrors sat embedded in the plan with no declared owner and nothing checking them. The registry is a const SURFACES inside the plan naming, for each surface, its ontology layer - branch workgraph, global workgraph, global ontology, observer, observe stage 05, design mirror, refraction surface - and the ONE skill that owns it. The Ecosystem Map tab renders the table straight from that array, so the registry cannot disagree with the page it describes. He also told me not to guess, and he was right: the definitions already existed in the plan's Refraction Surfaces table, recovered verbatim from the griot-ecosystem-map and refraction-pattern artifacts, and in the plan's own MERIDIAN array.

verification.evidence: const SURFACES (9 rows) + a ninth mirror tab for griot-ecosystem-map.html added to dgs-definitive-plan.html, matching the existing mirror markup (tab button, mirror-note, eager iframe, fallback card). Verified in chrome-devtools on the rendered page: tab label 'Ecosystem Map mirror', section visible, registry renders 9 rows, iframe src=griot-ecosystem-map.html loading=eager, 22 tabs, 9 mirror frames, 0 mojibake. Spec sourced from the plan's own Refraction Surfaces section and MERIDIAN array rather than invented.
verification.result: verified in a browser - 9 rows rendered from the array, not hand-written

nodes.title: tools/verify-surfaces.mjs - stage 4b, and the close of OA10
nodes.description: The gate that makes the registry mean something, and the Meridian stage the spine was missing. It reads SURFACES out of the plan itself and asserts, per surface: the file exists, the plan has a tab with that key, an eager iframe points at it, and it is committed. The two reflect-owned channels get a freshness check on the 4am day boundary by PARSING channel-going-dark and channel-day-surface and comparing the newest entry key - the parse doubles as a check that a broken block has not silently blanked the whole view. It also refuses to run if it parses fewer rows than the registry declares, because a gate that silently skips a row is worse than no gate. This closes OA10: griot-meridian-reflect is now held by the same spine as everything else.

verification.evidence: griot-live-artifacts/tools/verify-surfaces.mjs, wired as stage 4b of dgs-sync-all.ps1. First run failed honestly on a real condition, then on the corrected registry returned VERIFY_SURFACES_OK - 9 surfaces, briefing showing 'going-dark 2026-09-17 / day-surface 2026-09-17' read from parsed JSON. Full sync run reports 'surface registry + meridian OK 9 surfaces owned, embedded, current' and '9 frames, missing: none'.
verification.result: verified - the gate failed first, then passed on a real fix, which is the only proof that counts

nodes.title: I mistook a finished design mirror for stale data and nearly 'fixed' it
nodes.description: My first registry assigned meridian-day-surface.html to griot-meridian-reflect, so the gate reported it 44.8 days stale with no entry for today and told me to run the reflect. Wrong on both counts. That file is the design MIRROR of the day-surface view; the live dated data lives in the Briefing artifact's channel-day-surface block. The plan's own MERIDIAN array had already said so - owner 'design . dgs-plan-update', u '2026-07-19' - which is exactly the note Gavin told me existed and told me not to guess past. The file was finished, not stale. A gate built on a guessed owner manufactures work and erodes trust in every other row it prints.

verification.evidence: Parsed the briefing's channel blocks directly: channel-going-dark 31 entries newest 2026-09-17, channel-day-surface 34 entries newest 2026-09-17, briefings-archive 47 entries - all current. meridian-day-surface.html is 17,421 b, titled 'Meridian - day surface (Mirror)', and contains no channel-day-surface block at all. Registry corrected to layer 'design mirror' / owner 'dgs-plan-update'; the gate then returned VERIFY_SURFACES_OK with no work invented.
verification.result: verified by parsing both files - the disagreement was in my registry, not in the suite

nodes.title: The surface parser silently skipped a row and the count still looked plausible
nodes.description: One registry entry spells its name with double quotes because it contains an apostrophe - The Griot's Equation. The extraction regex only accepted single quotes, so that row vanished from the gate's output entirely. Eight rows printed, all green, nothing complained; the equation surface was simply not being checked. A validator that drops input silently is indistinguishable from one that passes it. Fixed by accepting both quote styles AND adding a self-check that counts declared rows against parsed rows and exits non-zero on a mismatch, so the next skipped row is loud instead of invisible.

verification.evidence: First run printed 8 rows (workgraph, ontology, drift, gold, dashboard, surface, briefing, ecomap) with no error; equation was absent. After the fix the run prints 9 including 'equation observer griot-equation 4.2d old'. The PARSE MISMATCH guard was added in the same change and exits 2 with the declared-vs-parsed counts.

nodes.title: The card check ran before the commit, so fresh edits read as in sync
nodes.description: Card freshness compares each live file against its published card by GIT COMMIT TIME, because mtime lies - a bulk copy resets it. But the stage ran before the push, so a file edited during the run but not yet committed still compared as byte-identical to a card that was about to be stale. It hid the drift codex on the run that re-rendered it: the gate said 87 in sync, 1 stale, and the drift card was quietly in the wrong bucket. Commit first, then check what the world can actually see.

verification.evidence: Reordered dgs-sync-all.ps1 to push -> cards -> report, with the reasoning written into the file as an ORDERING NOTE so it is not re-broken. The run immediately after reported DGS_SYNC_OK with 'artifact cards current: all in sync' only once the commit had actually landed, and the subsequent run correctly flagged dgs-definitive-plan as the single stale card after it was edited again.
verification.result: verified - the gate now flags on the next run what it previously hid

nodes.title: The card gate printed 'byte-identical' and never hashed a byte
nodes.description: verify-cards.ps1 opened by claiming it SHA-256s every live/*.html against its artifact card, and its summary line read 'in sync (byte-identical)'. It did neither - it compared FILE SIZE and MTIME. Because the Cowork publish pipeline injects a ~510-byte cowork-artifact-meta script block into every published card, a card is legitimately larger than its repo file, so two artifacts were parked in a 'card ahead of repo - inspect by hand, do NOT publish over' bucket from 2026-08-03. Six weeks, with byte-identical bodies the whole time. A gate that measures the wrong quantity does not merely miss drift - it manufactures phantom drift, and a permanent manual bucket is a bug report against the gate, not a standing task.

verification.evidence: Diffed both pairs by common prefix/suffix: repo 7,336 b == card 7,846 b minus a 510 b cowork-artifact-meta block (prefix 16 + suffix 7,320 = 7,336 exactly); the second pair identical in shape at 517 b. Fix strips the wrapper from both sides and SHA-256s the remaining body, short-circuiting before any size or mtime heuristic; the output label now reads 'body hash match' because that is what is measured. Re-run: 90 in sync, 0 stale, 0 missing, 0 card-ahead.
verification.result: verified - the manual bucket emptied without publishing over anything, which is the proof it was never real drift

nodes.title: The codex-plan-sync gate watched a path that has never existed
nodes.description: Stage 4 tested Prism/.prism/shared/workgraph/stories.json. The skill emits to .prism/stories/<epic>/stories.json. The tested path had never existed and never would, so the check could only ever take its else-branch and report OK with the words 'no stories.json yet - expected today'. I read that line three separate times today and repeated it back to Gavin as a known gap, which is exactly how a reassuring gate works: it is not passing on an absence, it is passing on a TYPO, permanently. A gate pointed at the wrong place is indistinguishable from no gate except that it stops you looking.

verification.evidence: Located the real store by search, then confirmed against the prism-codex-plan-sync SKILL.md which specifies '.prism/stories/stories.json with stable STORY-NNN ids' and 'stories.json (not plan checkboxes) is status truth'. Stage 4 repointed: absence of the store or an empty store now FAILS; age is reported per epic with a >30d callout that does NOT fail the run, because the plan changes most days and a permanently-red gate gets ignored - the same hole in a different shape. First honest run: 4 epic(s), 49 stories, oldest ceremony-review-audit-gate 57d.
verification.result: verified - four epics and 49 stories that no gate had ever looked at are now watched

nodes.title: The story-id conventions are the other way round - s-hash is contract-compliant, STORY-NNN is the deviation
nodes.description: Surfaced by a bug in my own fix: the first story counter matched /"id":\s*"STORY-/ and reported 0 stories for three of the four epics. They were not empty - they use older s-<hash8> ids. A shape-based count silently erases whatever does not match the shape, which is the same failure family as the parser that dropped The Griot's Equation earlier today. The real finding underneath: prism-codex-plan-sync specifies stable STORY-NNN ids precisely so status survives a re-decomposition, and only channel-adoption (25 stories) uses them. The root store, ceremony-review-audit-gate and prism-gavel predate the convention, so re-decomposing them would lose their status. Reported rather than silently normalised - renaming ids is Gavin's call, not a gate's.

verification.evidence: stories-contract.md rule 4 + _id_note read verbatim; workgraph-index.mjs header names STORY-001 as contract-forbidden Dialect B. dgs-sync-all.ps1 stage 4 labels corrected from 's-hash (pre-convention)' / 'STORY-NNN' to 's-hash (contract rule 4)' / 'STORY-NNN (dialect B)', with the correction and its cause written into the script. Ontology section 'find the CONTRACT before you modernise a format' propagated to all four surfaces.
verification.result: corrected - the rename was NOT performed, and the reason is recorded rather than the outcome quietly changed

correction.wasClaimed: Two story-id conventions coexist and only one is stable: prism-codex-plan-sync specifies stable STORY-NNN ids, and only channel-adoption uses them; the root store, ceremony-review-audit-gate and prism-gavel predate the convention with older s-hash ids, so re-decomposing them would lose their status.
correction.isTrue: Backwards. The stories contract rule 4 requires a content-hash id derived from the behavioral-requirement text - 'stable across re-emits, NOT a sequential label like STORY-001'. So s-<hash8> IS the compliant, genuinely stable form: an unchanged requirement keeps its id through an iterate_plan and its in-flight status survives. STORY-NNN is Dialect B, which the index generator absorbs as ids 'that the contract forbids'. channel-adoption is the epic out of step; the other three were right all along. The three epics I called pre-convention lose nothing on a re-decomposition - that is precisely what content-derived ids buy.
correction.cause: I took prism-codex-plan-sync's SKILL.md ('stable STORY-NNN ids') as the authority without reading the contract it is supposed to implement, and pattern-matched opaque hashes as legacy and sequential labels as modern. Tidier looked newer. Gavin then said 'you can rename' and I was one step from renumbering 24 compliant ids into the forbidden form - caught only by reading the index generator's header while scoping the migration.

nodes.title: Both post-push gates now measure the right thing in the right place
nodes.description: The two items left open at the end of the previous pass turned out to be the same defect wearing different clothes: a gate that reassures without checking. The card gate measured the wrong QUANTITY (size instead of content) and invented drift; the stories gate measured in the wrong PLACE (a path that never existed) and invented calm. Fixing both required no new infrastructure - only making each gate actually perform the check its own output claimed. The rules went into the ontology as one section, because the pair is the lesson: if the output says byte-identical, hash bytes; if it says a file is missing, check where that file actually lives.

verification.evidence: verify-cards.ps1 content-aware (Get-CardBody strips the publish wrapper, Get-Sha compares) -> 90 in sync / 0 stale / 0 missing / 0 card-ahead. dgs-sync-all.ps1 stage 4 repointed at .prism/stories -> 4 epic(s), 49 stories, per-epic convention and age. Ontology section 'a gate must measure the right thing, in the right place' (+2,793 b) propagated to GLOBAL, the compat mirror and .codex/AGENTS.md; dgs-plan-update SKILL.md Step 7c added to both copies (45,052 b each). Drift #57 and #58.
verification.result: verified - both gates re-run green on real measurements rather than proxies

nodes.title: Two authorities disagree on story ids - the skill contradicts the contract
nodes.description: prism-codex-plan-sync's SKILL.md instructs agents to emit 'stable STORY-NNN ids'. The stories contract (rule 4) says the opposite: a story id is a hash of its behavioral-requirement text, 'stable across re-emits, NOT a sequential label like STORY-001', and scripts/workgraph-index.mjs absorbs STORY-NNN as 'Dialect B's ids that the contract forbids'. The contract wins - so the SKILL.md line is the defect, and every future run of that skill will keep minting non-compliant ids until it is fixed. It cannot be fixed from this session: the live copy is the read-only plugin cache, and the canonical source is the prism-plugin repo, which is not cloned on this machine. Second, separate decision: channel-adoption (25 stories) already carries STORY-NNN and is the one epic out of step. Re-deriving its ids from requirement text is a real migration and must be done by the emitter, not by hand - a hand-minted hash that does not match what the emitter would produce on re-emit destroys the exact stability the ids exist for.

verification.evidence: .prism/shared/contracts/stories-contract.md rule 4 and its _id_note read verbatim. scripts/workgraph-index.mjs header names Dialect B's STORY-001 ids as contract-forbidden. The conflicting line lives at rpm/plugin_01DWVft1gxrUEx7KKr8vKtga/skills/prism-codex-plan-sync/SKILL.md ('emit .prism/stories/stories.json with stable STORY-NNN ids'); no prism-plugin clone exists under GriotApps/GriotProducts/GriotMeta, so it cannot be edited here. git grep confirms STORY-001 appears in Prism docs only as an illustrative label, never as a reference to channel-adoption's actual stories - so a future migration would not break external links.
verification.result: open - two concrete follow-ups named: fix the skill line in the prism-plugin repo, and decide on channel-adoption's 25 ids

nodes.title: The account skill snapshot Cowork loads was 220 lines behind the device - the structural cause of the POT_T error

nodes.title: The shelf-to-POT_T leak was 171 tools across 41 source videos, not 115 from one bad pass
nodes.description: POT_T is the ONE source for OSS since the 2026-09-03 sunset, but 171 tools on the sunset shelf had no POT_T row, spread across 41 different source videos - a long-standing leak, not one pass. The raw counts actively hid it: POT_T 1157 vs shelf 1263 reads as a gap of 106, because POT_T also holds 65 rows the shelf never had. nodes.title: The oss-inspo mirror already carried all 171 - so the fix was additive and stripped nothing
nodes.description: Doctrine says regenerate oss-inspo from POT_T. Done naively here that would have deleted any oss-inspo item lacking a POT_T row - Gavin's content. nodes.title: 331 oss-inspo items carry a placeholder instead of a real slug
nodes.description: 331 of 1341 oss-inspo items have no resolvable repo slug - they carry literal placeholders such as '- unverified (named in video)' or '- hosted (cloudflare workers ai)'. This is the bare-spoken-name class that video-oss-gate.py exists to fail loudly on. nodes.title: Both bridge directions cache - the dgs-plan-update exemption for the commit direction is wrong
nodes.description: dgs-plan-update Rule 2 step 4 says the stage cache is keyed by path but that cloud-to-device commit_files 'writes bytes directly and is not affected'. Both halves of that were disproven in one session. Commit direction: a rewrite to the same device path delivered the previous version - 1950 bytes in the container, 1905 on disk, reported written with no rejection, and the stale code then ran twice. Stage direction: a comparison silently read a copy staged earlier in the same session and reported the live plan card as in sync when it was a full commit behind, which nearly authorised a publish on a false premise.

verification.evidence: byte-length mismatch 1950 vs 1905 on the commit direction; and this pass, /mnt/user-data/uploads/.../dgs-definitive-plan.html dated 09:18 returned POT_T 1157 / ITEMS 1834 while the live artifact fetch returned the same - resolving against git HEAD instead showed the working file at ITEMS 1857.

nodes.title: CRLF phantom churn traced to system-level core.autocrlf with no .gitattributes
nodes.description: The recurring ~10-file phantom diff under live/ is not a mount quirk. git config reports core.autocrlf=true at the SYSTEM level, inherited by the repo, and griot-live-artifacts has no .gitattributes. So every checkout writes CRLF into the working tree and any tool that rewrites a file with LF manufactures a whole-file diff. Twelve files were confirmed CRLF-only this pass by comparing carriage-return-stripped hashes against git HEAD - zero real content at risk.

verification.evidence: git config --system core.autocrlf = true; repo core.autocrlf = true; .gitattributes absent. Per-file check: tr -d '\r' hash of the working copy equals the same hash of git HEAD for all twelve dirty files. git checkout restored them; tree now clean.
verification.result: flagged-not-fixed - working tree cleaned, but the generator is still armed and will re-dirty on the next Windows-side write. Repo policy is Gavin's call - see S8.

nodes.title: INV2 had one violation, not forty-five - and the one was a music mix, not a missing transcript
nodes.description: An in-session claim that 45 INV2 violations remained across three sessions was wrong: the count had been taken before the description-source backfill landed. The real figure was one, and the offending record was not an AI video at all - 'Gentle & Smooth R&B Mix in a Brooklyn Loft, Set 52, Ceema' had ridden into the AI News catch-up session with captions disabled, so it carried a digest with no backing transcript and no declared source. Also corrected in the same pass: the claim that the next batch had to wait about four hours. Only the timedtext door was blocked; the cdp door was clean at fail_streak 0, so the batch was never actually gated.

verification.evidence: bridge run: 'store: .../GriotApps/Cinopsis/data (canonical) -- 12 sessions' -> INV2 PASS. Native run: 'store: C:\Users\digit\.claude\plugins\data\cinopsis-cinopsis (canonical) -- 37 sessions' + 'store: ...GriotApps\Cinopsis\data -- 12 sessions' -> INV2 FAIL, 44 violations across 49 sessions; after syncing the 2026-09-02 description-backed digest into canonical, 43.

correction.wasClaimed: INV2 had ONE violation, not forty-five - and the earlier count of 45 was wrong because it predated the description-source backfill.

Run natively it enumerates TWO stores, adding the canonical plugin store at C:\Users\digit\.claude\plugins\data\cinopsis-cinopsis with 37 more sessions, for 49 sessions and 1378 digest entries. The gate was reporting honestly about a partial view; the surface it ran on silently narrowed the corpus. A count taken through the bridge is a count of the repo, never of the ecosystem.

nodes.title: Three independent faults each presented as the same symptom - 'all rungs failed'
nodes.description: The YT lane's failure looked like one problem and was three. F1: the cdp-panel rung was OPT-IN and nothing ever set CINOPSIS_ENABLE_CDP, so the rung built specifically to survive an IP flag had never run. nodes.title: Two bugs that reasoning could not have caught, and an agent that refused to claim done
nodes.description: The headless architect run implemented everything and then hit a permission wall on Bash/python. closureModel.rule: Lane closure is COMPUTED, never judged: a node counts closed if its state is in closedStates, open if in openStates. Both lists live here so the percentage is always auditable and a new state cannot silently change a number without being classified first.

readinessModel.rule: Readiness is a QUICK-CLOSE aid, not a decision. Five factors, 0-20 each, summed to 0-100, each stored separately and each tagged measured or judged so the number always decomposes. The LOWEST factor names the reason the item is not closed - that is the whole point.

factors.tooling: exists and reachable 20 | exists unreachable 10-12 | must be built 0
factors.blastRadius: INVERTED - one file 20 | one repo 12-16 | multi-repo 8 | cross-surface 0-4
factors.decisionDebt: no ruling needed 20 | one ruling 10 | unresolved conflict 0
